# yaml

Source: `quickjs-yaml.c` (module), `src/yaml/ywrite.c` + `include/yaml/ywrite.h` (writer) — flat function list.

Parses YAML into a plain JS value tree (`parse`, needs CYAML), and serializes one back to a small,
deterministic block-YAML subset (`write`, `stringify`): nested mappings/sequences via indentation,
plain or quoted scalars. The writer has no anchors/aliases, no multi-document streams, no flow style
(except the two exceptions noted below), no custom tags. Written for the eagle-agent library indexer
(`../eagle-agent.md`), which needs a compact, human- and LLM-readable source-of-truth text for the
EAGLE parts catalog — but it's general-purpose for any plain data tree.

## Build: CYAML is optional

`parse` is parsed by [CYAML](https://github.com/andrewmd5/cyaml) (YAML 1.2, MIT, no dependencies).
The module builds without it and then exports only `write` and `stringify`; a script that needs
`parse` can test `typeof yaml.parse`.

| `-DBUILD_LIBCYAML=` | CYAML | `parse` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AUTO` (default) | the installed one (`cyaml.h` + `libcyaml`), else none | only if found |
| `ON` | built from `third_party/cyaml` (cloned from git on first configure) | yes |
| `OFF` | not used | no |

`DEPS_BUILD=CMAKE` or `ALL` also builds a missing CYAML. `CYAML_PREFIX`, `CYAML_INCLUDE_DIR` and
`CYAML_LIBRARY_DIR` point at an installed copy that is not in the default paths.

## Functions

| Function | Args | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `parse(text)` | 1 | YAML text to a JS value. Several documents (`---`) give an array of them, an empty text gives `null`. Only with CYAML. |
| `stringify(value, replacer?, space?)` | 1 | As `write()`, with `Bun.YAML.stringify`'s signature: `space` is a number of spaces per level or a string whose length is used (max 10), default 2. A `replacer` other than `null`/`undefined` throws `TypeError`. |
| `write(value, indent?)` | 1 | Serializes `value` to a YAML string. `indent` is the number of spaces per nesting level, default `2`. Non-positive values fall back to the default. |

`stringify` differs from Bun in the output: Bun writes flow style (`{a: 1}`) when `space` is omitted,
this module always writes block style.

### `parse()` rules

| YAML | JS |
| --- | --- |
| plain `null`, `~`, empty | `null` |
| plain `true`/`false` (any case) | boolean |
| plain `12`, `0x1F`, `0o17`, `1.5e3`, `.inf`, `.nan` | number (an integer past int64 is a double) |
| quoted, block (`\|`, `>`) scalar, or a plain one with a tag other than the types below (`!!str 12`) | string |
| plain `!!int 5`, `!!float 1`, `!!bool true` | number, number, boolean (a text that is not one stays a string); `!!null` keeps the text's own type |
| mapping | plain object, keys in document order, a key is its text (`1:` is `"1"`, `~:` is `"null"`) |
| sequence | array |
| alias `*a` | **the same JS value** as the anchored node (so `r.y === r.x`, and `&a {b: *a}` is a cycle) |

Merge keys (`<<`) are an ordinary key, as in YAML 1.2. A mapping key that is not a scalar throws
`TypeError`; a syntax error throws `SyntaxError` with `line N, column M`; a non-string argument
throws `TypeError`.

```js
import { parse } from 'yaml';

parse('a: 1\nb: [x, true, ~]\n'); // { a: 1, b: ['x', true, null] }
parse('a: 1\n---\nb: 2\n');      // [{ a: 1 }, { b: 2 }]
```

## Translation rules

| JS value | YAML output |
| --- | --- |
| `null`, `undefined` | `null` |
| `true` / `false` | `true` / `false` |
| number | its JS string form (`42`, `3.14`, …) — unquoted; `NaN`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity` as `.nan`, `.inf`, `-.inf` |
| string | plain if unambiguous, else double-quoted (see below) |
| `{}` (empty object) | `{}` |
| `[]` (empty array) | `[]` |
| non-empty object | block mapping, keys in **JS insertion order** |
| non-empty array | block sequence |
| function, symbol, BigInt | throws `TypeError` |

**Empty `{}`/`[]` are the one deliberate flow-style exception** — block
style has no way to represent zero entries, so an empty collection is
always written as the flow literal, at any depth.

### Nesting

Every level of nesting adds one `indent`-width block of leading spaces.
A key's value starts on the same line if it's a scalar or empty
collection; a non-empty nested object/array starts on the **next** line,
indented one level deeper than the key. Array items that are themselves
non-empty objects/arrays are written as a bare `-` on its own line,
followed by the nested block indented one level deeper than the `-`:

```yaml
key: 1
list:
  - a
  - b
nested:
  a: 1
  b:
    - 1
    - 2
listOfMaps:
  -
    x: 1
  -
    y: 2
```

from:

```js
write({
  key: 1,
  list: ['a', 'b'],
  nested: { a: 1, b: [1, 2] },
  listOfMaps: [{ x: 1 }, { y: 2 }],
});
```

### Scalar quoting

A string is written **plain** (bare, no quotes) unless any of these hold,
in which case it's written **double-quoted** with JSON-style escapes
(`\"`, `\\`, `\n`, `\t`, `\r`, `\xHH` for other control bytes):

- empty string
- leading or trailing space
- starts with a YAML indicator character: `- ? : , [ ] { } # & * ! | > ' " % @` \` `` ` or whitespace
- contains `: ` (colon-space) or a bare trailing `:`, or ` #` (space-hash) — these are structurally significant in YAML
- contains any control character (byte < 0x20)
- looks like a number (`123`, `-1.5e10`, `0x1F`, `0o17`, `.inf`, `.nan`, …) — quoted so it stays a string on read-back
- matches a YAML 1.1 boolean/null keyword, case-sensitively against `null`/`Null`/`NULL`/`~`, `true`/`True`/`TRUE`, `false`/`False`/`FALSE`, `yes`/`Yes`/`YES`, `no`/`No`/`NO`, `on`/`On`/`ON`, `off`/`Off`/`OFF`

Everything else — including a string that merely *contains* a `"` or `'`
mid-word (`a "quote" here`) — is left unquoted; those characters are only
special at the start of a scalar.

**Practical implication for pin names:** EAGLE pin names like `RA0/AN0` or
`RB7/KBI3/PGD` are plain (no leading indicator char, no `: `/`#`, not
numeric/keyword-shaped) and come out unquoted. A bare pad number used as a
pin name (e.g. `"1"`, `"2"` for a resistor) looks numeric and **will** be
quoted — keep that in mind if a consumer expects a raw string.

## Worked example: an EAGLE parts-catalog entry

Given a condensed deviceset record built as a plain JS object (matching
the fields `eagle-agent.md` §1 wants — name, prefix, description, gate →
pin list, package variants):

```js
import { write } from 'yaml';

const catalog = {
  'mcu.lbr': {
    'PIC18F2550-I/SP': {
      prefix: 'U',
      packages: ['SPDIP28'],
      pins: ['RA0/AN0', 'RA1/AN1', 'VDD', 'VSS'],
    },
  },
  'r.lbr': {
    R: { prefix: 'R', pins: ['1', '2'] },
  },
};

print(write(catalog));
```

produces:

```yaml
mcu.lbr:
  PIC18F2550-I/SP:
    prefix: U
    packages:
      - SPDIP28
    pins:
      - RA0/AN0
      - RA1/AN1
      - VDD
      - VSS
r.lbr:
  R:
    prefix: R
    pins:
      - "1"
      - "2"
```

Note the quoted `"1"`/`"2"`: those pin names are digit-only strings, so
the numeric-lookalike rule quotes them to keep them strings.

## Caveats for callers

- Build the plain object/array tree first (e.g. from `eagle.js`'s
  `EagleDocument` getters), then hand the finished tree to `write()` in
  one call — there's no streaming/incremental writer.
- Key order is whatever order you assigned object properties in; if
  ordering matters for the catalog's readability (e.g. `prefix` before
  `pins`), build the object literal in that order.
- `write()` throws `TypeError` on functions, symbols and BigInts in the tree, and on a value that contains itself (nesting past 1000 levels) — strip or convert
  those before calling it.

# digest

Source: `quickjs-digest.c` — module exports **`digest`**, **`algorithms`**

One-shot message digests: md5, sha1 and the SHA-2 family. The engine under [node-crypto](../js/node-crypto.md). It wraps [th-blitz/Hash-Algorithms](https://github.com/th-blitz/Hash-Algorithms) (MIT, a git submodule in `third_party/Hash-Algorithms`, pinned to 953a0b6), which hashes a whole message at once, so chunking is the caller's job.

```js
import { digest, algorithms } from 'digest';

digest('sha256', new TextEncoder().encode('abc')); // ArrayBuffer, 32 bytes
```

| Export | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `digest(algorithm, data)` | `data` is an `ArrayBuffer` or any view, the result an `ArrayBuffer` of the digest size. `algorithm` is a lowercase name from `algorithms`. Throws `TypeError` for other data, `RangeError` for an unknown algorithm. |
| `algorithms` | Array of `{ name, size, blockSize }`: md5 (16, 64), sha1 (20, 64), sha224 (28, 64), sha256 (32, 64), sha384 (48, 128), sha512 (64, 128), sha512-224 (28, 128), sha512-256 (32, 128). |

## Notes

- The library reads the message as 32 or 64 bit words. `digest()` copies a message that is not 8-byte aligned (a view at an odd offset) before hashing.
- Digest words are written big-endian explicitly, but the library itself reads message words as little-endian: no big-endian hosts.
- Built when `MODULE_DIGEST=ON` (the default) and the submodule is checked out; its sources are compiled into `libmodules.a`.

/* helpers behind skip(), on (p, n) views
 *
 *   js_path_comp   length of the component at p (from pos)
 *   js_path_sep    length of the separator run at p
 *   js_path_skip   component plus the separators after it
 */
static inline size_t
js_path_comp(const char* p, size_t len, size_t pos) {
  const char *start = p, *end = p + len;

  if(pos > len)
    pos = len;
  p += pos;
  while(p < end && !path_issep(*p))
    ++p;
  return p - start;
}

static inline size_t
js_path_sep(const char* p, size_t len) {
  const char *start = p, *end = p + len;

  while(p < end && path_issep(*p))
    ++p;
  return p - start;
}

static inline size_t
js_path_skip(const char* s, size_t n) {
  const char *p = s, *e = s + n;

  p += js_path_comp(s, n, 0);
  p += js_path_sep(p, e - p);
  return p - s;
}

/* Node's path.dirname length (not POSIX: the separator run before the basename loses one
 * byte only), 0 for "."
 *
 *   "/tmp/x" -> 4    "/foo" -> 1    "a//b" -> 2 ("a/")    "//a" -> 2
 */
static size_t
js_path_dirlen(const char* path, size_t n) {
  int hasroot, matched = 1;
  ssize_t end = -1, i;

  if(n == 0)
    return 0;

  hasroot = path_issep(path[0]);

  for(i = n - 1; i >= 1; --i) {
    if(path_issep(path[i])) {
      if(!matched) {
        end = i;
        break;
      }
    } else {
      matched = 0;
    }
  }

  if(end == -1)
    return hasroot ? 1 : 0;

  return hasroot && end == 1 ? 2 : end;
}

/* extension of a[0..n) per Node's path.extname: `pos` is the offset of the dot (n if none),
 * `len` the bytes from it to the end of the basename
 *
 *   "a/b.tar.gz" -> ".gz"    ".bashrc" -> none    "a.txt/" -> ".txt"
 */
static size_t
js_path_extpos(const char* a, size_t n) {
  return path_extoff(a, n);
}

static size_t
js_path_extlen(const char* a, size_t n) {
  size_t off = path_extoff(a, n), bl;
  const char* b = path_basename(a, n, &bl);

  return off == n ? 0 : (size_t)(b - a) + bl - off;
}

/* basename of a[0..n) as Node's path.basename sees it: `*len` bytes at the returned
 * offset; empty for "" and for a path of only separators
 *
 *   "/tmp/test/" -> pos 5 len 4    "/" -> pos 1 len 0
 */
static size_t
js_path_basename(const char* a, size_t n, size_t* len) {
  const char* b = path_basename(a, n, len);

  if(*len && path_issep(*b)) {
    *len = 0;
    return n;
  }

  return b - a;

/* normalizes p[0..n) into `db` the way Node's path.normalize does: "" is ".", a
 * trailing separator stays
 *
 *   "a//b/../c/" -> "a/c/"    "" -> "."
 */
static void
js_path_normalize(const char* p, size_t n, DynBuf* db) {
  size_t w;

  db->size = 0;

  if(dbuf_claim(db, n + 4))
    return;

  w = path_canon((char*)db->buf, db->allocated_size, p, n);
  db->size = w;

  if(n && path_issep(p[n - 1]) && w && !path_issep(db->buf[w - 1]))
    dbuf_putc(db, PATHSEP_C);

  dbuf_0(db);
}

 * (what path.absolute does)

static void
js_path_absolute(const char* p, size_t n, DynBuf* db) {
  DynBuf tmp;

  dbuf_init2(&tmp, 0, 0);

  if(!path_isabs(p, n) && path_getcwd(&tmp) && tmp.size) {
    if(n && tmp.buf[tmp.size - 1] != PATHSEP_C)
      dbuf_putc(&tmp, PATHSEP_C);

  js_path_normalize((const char*)tmp.buf, tmp.size, db);

 *                      // The "path" argument must be of type string. Received type number (5)
 * ```
 *
 *   JSValueConst  v         the rejected argument
 *   const char*   name      parameter name for the message: "path", "suffix", "paths[1]", ...
 *   const char*   expected  "string" or "object"
 *

static int
js_path_invalid_arg(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst v, const char* name, const char* expected) {
  JSValue err, tmp;
  const char* s;
  DynBuf db = DBUF_INIT_CTX(ctx);

  dbuf_printf(&db, "The \"%s\" argument must be of type %s. Received ", name, expected);

  if(JS_IsUndefined(v))
    dbuf_putstr(&db, "undefined");
  else if(JS_IsNull(v))
    dbuf_putstr(&db, "null");
  else if(JS_IsFunction(ctx, v)) {
    tmp = JS_GetPropertyStr(ctx, v, "name");
    s = JS_IsString(tmp) ? JS_ToCString(ctx, tmp) : 0;
    dbuf_printf(&db, "function %s", s ? s : "");
    if(s)
      JS_FreeCString(ctx, s);
    JS_FreeValue(ctx, tmp);
  } else if(JS_IsObject(v)) {
    JSValue ctor = JS_GetPropertyStr(ctx, v, "constructor");

    tmp = JS_IsObject(ctor) ? JS_GetPropertyStr(ctx, ctor, "name") : JS_UNDEFINED;
    s = JS_IsString(tmp) ? JS_ToCString(ctx, tmp) : 0;
    dbuf_printf(&db, "an instance of %s", s && *s ? s : "Object");
    if(s)
      JS_FreeCString(ctx, s);
    JS_FreeValue(ctx, tmp);
    JS_FreeValue(ctx, ctor);
  } else {
    /* Symbol(x) cannot go through ToString: String(v) does it */
    JSValue g = JS_GetGlobalObject(ctx), str = JS_GetPropertyStr(ctx, g, "String");

    tmp = JS_Call(ctx, str, JS_UNDEFINED, 1, &v);
    s = JS_IsString(tmp) ? JS_ToCString(ctx, tmp) : 0;
    dbuf_printf(&db,
                "type %s (%s%s)",
                JS_IsNumber(v)        ? "number"
                : JS_IsBool(v)        ? "boolean"
                : JS_IsBigInt(ctx, v) ? "bigint"
                                      : "symbol",
                s ? s : "",
                JS_IsBigInt(ctx, v) ? "n" : "");
    if(s)
      JS_FreeCString(ctx, s);
    JS_FreeValue(ctx, tmp);
    JS_FreeValue(ctx, str);
    JS_FreeValue(ctx, g);

  dbuf_0(&db);
  JS_ThrowTypeError(ctx, "%s", (const char*)db.buf);
  dbuf_free(&db);

  JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, err, "code", JS_NewString(ctx, "ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE"));

# path

Source: `quickjs-path.c` — module exports a flat list of functions.

Filesystem path manipulation (Node `path`-like, with extra POSIX helpers). Most
functions take a path string as the first argument.

The Node functions (`basename`, `dirname`, `extname`, `format`, `isAbsolute`, `join`, `normalize`, `parse`,
`relative`, `resolve`) throw `TypeError` with `code: 'ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE'` and Node's message for a
non-string argument (`basename` also for a non-string `suffix`, `relative` also for a missing `to`).
The other functions coerce their arguments to strings.

`toNamespacedPath(path)` returns `path` unchanged (POSIX); `_makeLong` is the same function. `path/posix`
and `node:path/posix` import this module.

## Components & names

| Function | Args | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `basename(path)` | 1 | Final path component. |
| `dirname(path)` | 1 | Directory portion of the path. |
| `extname(path)` | 1 | File extension (with dot). |
| `skip(path, pos?)` | 1 | Offset after the component at `pos` and its separators, `-1` at the end. |

## Filesystem queries

| Function | Args | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exists(path)` | 1 | Whether the path exists. Follows symlinks like `fs.existsSync`: a dangling link is `false`. |
| `isAbsolute(path)` | 1 | Whether the path starts at the root; `!isAbsolute(p)` for a relative one. |
| `isDirectory` / `isFile` / `isSymlink` | 1 | Type predicates on the `S_IF*` bits. `isDirectory` and `isFile` follow symlinks (`stat`, like `fs.statSync`), `isSymlink` tests the link itself (`lstat`). `false` if the entry is missing. Other types: `fs.statSync(p).isFIFO()` and the like. |
| `getcwd(buf)` | 1 | Current working directory. |
| `gethome(buf)` | 1 | Home directory. |
| `fnmatch(pattern)` | 1 | Glob-style pattern match. |

## Normalization (return newly built strings)

| Function | Args | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `normalize(path)` | 1 | Normalizes separators and `.`/`..`. |
| `realpath(path)` | 1 | Resolves all symlinks. |
| `relative(from, to)` | 2 | Relative path from `from` to `to`. |

## Node-style helpers

| Function | Args | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `join(...parts)` | 1 | Joins components with the separator. |
| `parse(path)` | 1 | Returns `{root, dir, base, ext, name}`. |
| `format(obj)` | 1 | Inverse of `parse`. |
| `resolve(...parts)` | 1 | Resolves to an absolute path from segments. |

## Constants

`delimiter` (path-list separator) and `sep` (path separator) strings.

## posix and default export

`path.posix` and the default export are the module's own functions (`import path from
'path'`; `path.posix === path`). There is no `path.win32`. `join()` does not normalize
(`join('a', '..', 'b')` is `'a/../b'`, Node gives `'b'`) and an absolute argument restarts
the result.

| `absolute(p)` | `resolve(p)` |
